differencesRecorded: An .mp3 name: retail reads the foreign .mp3 twice, then the English .wav and .mp3; Fn reads the foreign .mp3, .wav, .ogg, then the English .mp3, .wav, .ogg. They differ only for a voice in both formats or a foreign .wav asked for as .mp3: no installed voice is in both formats, and the three Spanish WAVs are asked for as .wav.
Fn finds "chars" in any case without lowercasing the rest of the name; pak lookups ignore case, so the same file loads. Fn's OpenAL backend lowercases every name anyway.
The Ogg Vorbis attempt after .mp3 is Fn's own, as for every name.
The data-build pass (com_buildScript) is not reproduced.
With developer set, Fn's fallback note names the foreign file read; retail prints nothing.
